solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: German citizen's meaty snack

definitions.meaning: in German the word for a townsman or citizen is spelt like the snack, with an umlaut; the 's links
a patty of minced meat in a bun

explanation.surface: A sly dig suggesting what a German eats for lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Bürger is the German word for a townsman, and a burger is a beef patty in a bun, so one spelling covers both.

clue.text: A local lass

parts.note: read cryptically, a local is a pub, and the lass of the pub serves behind its bar

explanation.walkthrough: 'local' looks like a neighbourhood girl, but in Britain the local is your nearest pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman serving drinks at a pub is a young woman of the local, one who works the bar.

clue.text: Bread maker represented normality

indicators.note: represented, read as re-presented, means the letters of normality are set out afresh

explanation.surface: A baker presented as the very picture of normality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread' is slang for money; the Royal Mint makes Britain's coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is slang for money, and the Royal Mint manufactures the UK's coinage.

clue.text: Greatly exaggerated at the start on the left-hand page

indicators.note: at the start means only the opening letter of exaggerated is taken

parts.note: the verso is the left-hand page of an open book

explanation.surface: A book's opening page is wildly overstated.
explanation.definitionFit: Ever so is a colloquial intensifier meaning very much, as in ever so grateful.

clue.text: Guarantee Bill with loan

parts.note: AC is the abbreviation for account, a bill
credit is money lent, a loan

explanation.surface: A banker securing a bill against a loan.
explanation.definitionFit: To accredit is to vouch for or officially recognise, which amounts to guaranteeing.

clue.text: Cabbage and King

definitions.meaning: an old word for cabbage and related brassicas, as in coleslaw
Old King ... is the merry old soul of the nursery rhyme

explanation.definitionFit: Cole names brassica plants like kale, and Cole is the monarch of the children's rhyme.

clue.text: Comfy chair from ruin, we're told, on cruise ship

indicators.note: we're told means the word for ruin is heard, not spelt

parts.note: wreck means ruin
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: Finding an easy chair amid the ruins on board a holiday ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A recliner is an armchair whose back tilts so you can lie back in comfort.

clue.text: Live and prosper, losing nothing

indicators.note: losing means the letter for nothing is taken out of the phrase

parts.note: do well means prosper
O, the round zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: The Vulcan farewell, live long and prosper, missing a word.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes Star Trek's Vulcan greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell somewhere is to reside there, to live in it.

clue.text: Siamese attacks reported, bringing strings of invectives

indicators.note: reported means the phrase for Siamese attacks is spoken aloud

parts.note: Siam is the old name for Thailand, so Siamese means Thai; raids are attacks

explanation.surface: A news report on Thai military strikes provoking angry outbursts.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirade is a long angry speech, a stream of abuse or denunciation.

clue.text: Spoke of Frost's poems

indicators.note: spoke of says the word for frosts is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: rime is hoar frost, so frosts are rimes

explanation.surface: Someone talking about the verse of the poet Robert Frost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frost's' looks like the American poet; it is the plural of frost, RIMES, which is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhymes are short verses, especially nursery verse, so they are poems.

clue.text: Regular daily local repairs — the panic's over

indicators.note: regular means taking every second letter, evenly spaced, from the words that follow

explanation.surface: Relief that the neighbourhood's routine repairs mean the crisis has passed.
explanation.definitionFit: The all clear is the signal, as after an air raid, that danger has gone and people can relax.

clue.text: He won't appreciate being by the fire

definitions.meaning: someone ungrateful, who does not appreciate favours
read as ..., sitting in the fireplace

explanation.surface: Someone who's ungrateful for a warm seat by the hearth.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer as IN GRATE, a grate being the iron basket holding a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingrate is an ungrateful person, one who fails to value kindness shown to him.

clue.text: 1961 UK Eurovision duo giving Everyone, My Boys

parts.note: all means everyone
the setter's 'my' points to I, the setter, so my boys are I's sons
boys are sons

explanation.surface: A parent proudly naming their sons after a pop group.
explanation.walkthrough: The Allisons were a British pop duo who came second for the UK at the 1961 Eurovision Song Contest with Are You Sure?
explanation.definitionFit: The Allisons were the act that represented the United Kingdom at Eurovision in 1961, a pair of singers.

clue.text: Plundered centre of Uxbridge — then ran off

indicators.note: centre of means the middle two letters of the eight-letter word Uxbridge

parts.note: fled means ran off

explanation.surface: A looter sacks a London suburb's town centre and escapes.
explanation.walkthrough: Uxbridge is a town in west London.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle a place is to ransack it, searching and stealing, so rifled means plundered.

clue.text: Wraps biro holders, dropping bit of paper

indicators.note: dropping means a letter is left out of the pen holders

parts.note: a Biro is a ballpoint pen

indicators.note: bit of means just the first letter of paper

parts.note: cases are holders

explanation.surface: Packing pen cases while losing a scrap of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To encase something is to enclose it completely, so encases means wraps or covers.

clue.text: Welshmen's platform

definitions.meaning: Dai is a stock Welsh man's name; read with the 's, Welshmen is the plural
a raised stage at the end of a hall

explanation.surface: A stage or rostrum belonging to some men from Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A dais is a raised floor at one end of a hall, a platform for speakers.

clue.text: More than one cordial aged senora stirred

indicators.note: stirred means the letters of aged senora are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: An elderly Spanish lady mixing several drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Orangeades are fruit drinks, and a cordial is a sweet soft drink, so several cordials.

clue.text: Past blooming, damage to red leaf

indicators.note: damage means the letters of to red leaf are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Frost harming a red leaf after the flowers have gone.
explanation.definitionFit: A deflorate plant has shed its flowers, so it is no longer in flower.

clue.text: Info about leading industrialist working at railway buildings

indicators.note: about means the info word goes around the other letters

parts.note: stats, statistics, are information

indicators.note: leading means just the first letter of industrialist

parts.note: on means working, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: Gathering data on a rail tycoon who works at the depots.
explanation.definitionFit: Stations are the stopping places with platforms and buildings where trains pick up passengers.

clue.text: Postman's knock?

parts.note: the sound a postman makes rapping on the door; Postman's Knock is also a kissing party game

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the cryptic reading: the game name read literally as the noise of a postman knocking.
explanation.definitionFit: The repeated tapping sound of someone rapping at a door is what the imitative word renders.

clue.text: Go berserk and take the Reds back. All right

parts.note: R stands for recipe, Latin for take, on prescriptions

indicators.note: back means the football club's short name is written backwards

parts.note: the Reds is the nickname of Manchester United, Man U
OK means all right

explanation.surface: A football fan going wild about taking back the Reds.
explanation.walkthrough: Manchester United, Man U, are an English football club nicknamed the Reds.
explanation.definitionFit: To run amok is an idiom for behaving wildly and violently, out of control.

clue.text: Nadal returns from a distance

indicators.note: returns means the tennis player's first name is read backwards

parts.note: Rafa is the familiar first name of tennis player Rafael Nadal

explanation.surface: A tennis star hitting returns from deep behind the baseline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' looks like a tennis stroke but it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar means at or from a long way off, as in seen from afar.

clue.text: Prompted again to keep shilling that's saved

indicators.note: to keep means the prompt word holds the coin letter inside it

parts.note: to cue is to prompt, so recued is prompted again
S is the abbreviation for shilling, an old British coin

explanation.surface: An actor given a second prompt and paid to stay, so the play was saved.
explanation.walkthrough: The shilling was a pre-decimal British coin worth twelve pence, written s.
explanation.definitionFit: To rescue someone is to deliver them from danger, so rescued means saved.

clue.text: Negotiate breaking one's standards

indicators.note: breaking means the bargain word bursts into the middle of the other

parts.note: one is I, so one's is I's
to deal is to negotiate

explanation.surface: Haggling that compromises one's principles.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideals are principles or models of excellence, the standards one aims for.

clue.text: Not far away from some fine art object

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A gallery visitor standing close to a piece of fine art.
explanation.definitionFit: Near to describes something close by, a short distance off.

clue.text: This psychotherapist takes on poor Leonard

indicators.note: takes means the letters of on are taken away from those of Leonard
poor means the remaining letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A therapist accepting a needy patient called Leonard.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove O and N from LEONARD and rearrange LEARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Adler was the Austrian psychotherapist who founded individual psychology.

clue.text: Beads expected, it's said, by falls

indicators.note: it's said means the word for expected is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: due means expected, as a train is due
drops means falls

explanation.surface: Someone predicting a necklace will end up near a waterfall.
explanation.definitionFit: Dewdrops are small round drops of moisture, beads of water on grass.

clue.text: Joined by a thread from all quarters

definitions.meaning: stitched together with needle and thread
read as the four compass points south, east, west and north in turn

explanation.surface: A garment stitched together from every direction.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is less a definition than the letters spelt out: the abbreviations for the four quarters of the compass.
explanation.definitionFit: Stitching fastens fabric with needle and thread, so the past participle means joined that way.

clue.text: Think about island deliveries

parts.note: Mull is an island in the Inner Hebrides off Scotland
in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries by one bowler

explanation.surface: Pondering how parcels reach a remote island.
explanation.walkthrough: Mull is a Scottish island; an over is a block of six balls bowled in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: To mull over is to ponder a matter at length, an idiom for thinking something through.

clue.text: Musical seen in Texan ad, unusually

indicators.note: seen in says the answer is visible inside the following words, running across them

explanation.surface: A stage show oddly spotted in a Texas advertisement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' looks like an anagram signal, but it only supplies the final letter of the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: Xanadu is a stage musical based on the 1980 roller-disco film starring Olivia Newton-John.

clue.text: Oil treatment for sore knee

indicators.note: treatment for means the letters of sore knee are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Rubbing oil into an aching joint as a remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Kerosene is paraffin, a fuel oil distilled from petroleum.

clue.text: Dances around on the up?

indicators.note: around means the letters of dances are turned about into another order

explanation.surface: Wondering if dancing in circles means things are improving.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascend is to climb, to go upward; the question mark admits the stretch from a verb to the phrase.
